citationData.scope: Citations between papers in this map
citationData.note: References to the official LZ preprint are normalized to arXiv:2609.02823.

papers.title: Search for dark matter particle interactions in an extended nuclear recoil energy window with the LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) experiment
papers.summary: LZ extends its nuclear-recoil search to roughly 270 keV and reports one event consistent with a 248 ± 23 (stat) ± 23 (sys) keV recoil. The maximum local significance is 3.4σ and the global significance is 2.6σ.
papers.takeaway: The experimental anchor: one unusual event, interesting enough to investigate but well below the threshold for a discovery.

papers.title: Inelastic Dark Matter Signature at High Recoil Energy in LUX-ZEPLIN and CRESST
papers.summary: Heavy halo dark matter scatters into a more massive state. A splitting near 350 keV suppresses lower-energy events, and the preferred region could be tested by a planned CRESST upgrade.
papers.takeaway: A generic endothermic explanation that shifts the recoil toward LZ's high-energy window.

papers.title: Higgsino Above the Sea of Fog
papers.summary: A thermal 1.1 TeV Higgsino with a several-hundred-keV neutral-state splitting can reach the event, though the rate depends strongly on the uncertain high-speed tail of the Galactic halo.
papers.takeaway: Places the event in a minimal thermal-Higgsino setting and emphasizes its astrophysical sensitivity.

papers.title: Higgsino Dark Matter Interpretation of the LUX-ZEPLIN 248 keV Nuclear-Recoil Event
papers.summary: A nearly pure, roughly 1 TeV Higgsino up-scatters through an off-diagonal Z coupling. The mass and interaction rate are largely fixed, leaving the neutral-state splitting to place the recoil.
papers.takeaway: A predictive Higgsino interpretation with less freedom than a generic inelastic model.

papers.title: TeV Higgsino Dark Matter from LZ Nuclear Recoil to Fermi-LAT Gamma Rays
papers.summary: A 1.1 TeV inelastic Higgsino is connected to a mild Fermi-LAT Galactic-center preference and to future gamma-ray tests with H.E.S.S. and CTAO.
papers.takeaway: Connects a Higgsino fit of LZ to independent indirect-detection channels.

papers.title: Fermionic Dark Matter Absorption and the High-Energy Event in LUX-ZEPLIN
papers.summary: Absorption of a roughly 247 MeV fermionic dark-matter particle on xenon converts its rest mass into a nearly monoenergetic recoil. The required benchmark is reported to be in strong tension with a KamLAND recast.
papers.takeaway: A distinct absorption mechanism that naturally lands at 248 keV but faces an important external constraint.

papers.title: A PQ-Symmetric High-Scale SUSY Interpretation of the LZ High-Energy Recoil
papers.summary: A 1.08 TeV Higgsino with a 0.3–0.35 MeV splitting is embedded in high-scale supersymmetry with a Peccei–Quinn sector and mixed Higgsino–axion dark matter.
papers.takeaway: Explains how the small Higgsino splitting might arise inside a broader high-scale theory.

papers.title: Dark Matter as the Z₂ Partner of the Standard Model Higgs Boson
papers.summary: An electroweak scalar doublet with a roughly 350 keV splitting produces the recoil through a fixed off-diagonal Z interaction and predicts pronounced annual modulation.
papers.takeaway: A non-Higgsino electroweak doublet with a sharp, testable seasonal prediction.

papers.title: Dark Matter at the Kinematic Edge: Interpreting the 248 keV LZ Nuclear-Recoil Candidate
papers.summary: A broad comparison finds ordinary elastic spin-independent scattering poorly suited to the isolated recoil, while spin-dependent and endothermic interactions remain viable. It develops pseudo-Dirac and thermal-Higgsino benchmarks.
papers.takeaway: A bridge between operator-level fits and concrete particle models with cosmological constraints.

papers.title: Strong Constraints on Higgsino Dark Matter from Solar Capture
papers.summary: The authors combine capture and annihilation in the Sun with IceCube's null result to argue for a splitting above 566 keV, which would exclude the thermal-Higgsino interpretation of the LZ event.
papers.takeaway: A direct challenge to the Higgsino island using solar capture and neutrino-telescope data.

papers.title: A Peccei-Quinn Origin for Inelastic Electroweak Dark Matter after LUX-ZEPLIN
papers.summary: Peccei–Quinn breaking splits a vectorlike electroweak doublet. The resulting subcomponent of dark matter can explain the recoil while axions provide the remaining abundance.
papers.takeaway: A mixed axion–electroweak scenario with a possible luminous signal.

papers.title: Inelastic Dark Photon Dark Matter for the LUX-ZEPLIN High-Recoil Event and the Galactic Halo Gamma-Ray Excess
papers.summary: A 420 GeV dark photon up-scatters to a heavier vector partner through a scalar mediator. The same sector is arranged to retain a proposed explanation of a Galactic halo gamma-ray excess.
papers.takeaway: Links the LZ recoil to a second anomaly using inelastic dark-photon dark matter.

papers.title: Sub-TeV Singlino Dark Matter in light from Sagittarius A* and LUX-ZEPLIN Nuclear-Recoil Event
papers.summary: The paper discusses a sub-TeV NMSSM singlino in relation to LZ, but concentrates on gamma-ray detectability near black-hole dark-matter spikes rather than a detailed recoil fit.
papers.takeaway: Kept at the coastline because its connection to the LZ recoil is suggestive rather than a comparable quantitative fit.

papers.title: Inelastic Signatures of Electroweak Dark Matter
papers.summary: Coupled Majorana and Dirac electroweak multiplets generate a neutral-state splitting and off-diagonal Z interaction. Matching one event selects representation-dependent thermal benchmarks and correlated low-energy signals.
papers.takeaway: Generalizes the electroweak mechanism beyond a single representation and exposes correlated predictions.

papers.title: TeV Higgsino Interpretation of the LZ High-Recoil Event with Intermediate-Scale Electroweak Gauginos
papers.summary: A GUT-scale bino–wino cancellation yields the required Higgsino splitting with a wino near 120 TeV. The construction also discusses the newly raised solar-capture constraints.
papers.takeaway: A UV-level response to how a Higgsino could acquire the required small splitting.

papers.title: Confronting the Higgsino Interpretation of the LZ Event with the High-Energy Sideband
papers.summary: The authors argue that a full-density thermal Higgsino should also populate an empty higher-energy sideband. The strength of the tension depends on acceptance information that is not yet public.
papers.takeaway: A second major challenge to the thermal-Higgsino reading, focused on LZ's own sideband.

papers.title: Seasonal dark matter from the LUX-ZEPLIN high-energy event
papers.summary: Generic endothermic dark matter near the halo's kinematic edge can fit the event and should modulate annually by more than 50%, reaching nearly 100% in some regions.
papers.takeaway: Turns the fragile halo-tail dependence into a strong seasonal test.

papers.title: Atmospheric neutrino up-scattering explanation of LZ 2026 excess
papers.summary: Instead of halo dark matter, an atmospheric neutrino up-scatters on a nucleus to create a new massive state. The kinematic threshold removes lower-energy recoils while leaving an isolated high-energy event.
papers.takeaway: The incoming particle is an atmospheric neutrino rather than Galactic dark matter.

papers.title: Axion Portal Dark Matter and the LUX-ZEPLIN High-Recoil Event
papers.summary: A momentum-dependent pseudoscalar interaction produces elastic nuclear recoils without relying on an inelastic state change. A light pseudoscalar mediator embeds the operator in an axion-portal model.
papers.takeaway: Shows how elastic scattering can still favor high recoil when the interaction is momentum suppressed at low energy.

papers.title: Exothermic and Endothermic Inelastic Dark Matter Interpretations at LZ: Sideband Constraints and Future Prospects
papers.summary: The paper compares down-scattering, which can make a sharp recoil feature, with broader endothermic spectra and uses the empty high-energy sideband to separate and constrain them.
papers.takeaway: A bridge between the two inelastic coasts and the strongest current spectral discriminant.

papers.title: Exothermic Dark Matter at LZ
papers.summary: A heavier dark state down-scatters and releases a 0.5–1 MeV splitting, allowing 30–200 GeV dark matter to make a high-energy recoil. The model predicts still-higher-energy events in argon and germanium.
papers.takeaway: A concrete dark-photon realization of down-scattering with multi-target predictions.

papers.title: Inelastic from the Other Side: Xenon Excitation Signals in Light of the LZ High-Recoil Event
papers.summary: The authors calculate accompanying xenon nuclear-excitation signals for high-recoil models. Expected rates are generally at or below roughly ten percent of the elastic rate, so much larger exposures are needed.
papers.takeaway: Not a competing cause, but a possible future way to diagnose high-recoil dark-matter models.

papers.title: Exothermic dark matter and the 248 keV nuclear recoil in LUX-ZEPLIN
papers.summary: The authors model the candidate as exothermic downscattering of an excited pseudo-Dirac state, arguing that its rate is comparatively insensitive to the halo escape speed and predicting several argon events per tonne-year near 250 keV.
papers.takeaway: An exothermic benchmark with an argon discriminator and a long-lived excited-state requirement.

papers.title: Inelastic dark matter and baryon flavor symmetry in light of LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) experiment
papers.summary: The author embeds TeV-scale inelastic dark matter in a broken baryon-flavor gauge symmetry and identifies parameters that reproduce the LZ recoil and relic density while satisfying existing collider and indirect-detection bounds.
papers.takeaway: Connects the required splitting to baryon flavor and predicts a relatively light weakly coupled gauge boson.

papers.title: The Inert Doublet Model of Dark Matter and the LUX-ZEPLIN High-Recoil Event
papers.summary: The authors test the inert-doublet model with the LZ event likelihood and find a viable high-mass region, with a reported best fit near 1.08 TeV and a 369 keV splitting between the neutral scalars.
papers.takeaway: A scalar electroweak-doublet realization of the near-threshold inelastic interpretation.

papers.title: Multi-Messenger and Paleo-Detector Probes of the LZ Dark Matter Signal
papers.summary: The authors fit a leptophobic inelastic model to the event, find no accompanying Fermi-LAT excess and consistency with IceCube, and estimate an approximately 80 nm recoil track that could be sought in lead-bearing paleo-detectors.
papers.takeaway: Extends an inelastic fit into multi-messenger null tests and a paleo-detector prediction.

papers.title: GUT-induced FCC signatures of the LUX-ZEPLIN event
papers.summary: The authors connect the pseudo-Dirac splitting suggested by the LZ event to an SU(6) grand-unified construction and argue that the associated tens-of-TeV gauge boson would be discoverable at a future 100 TeV hadron collider.
papers.takeaway: Turns the inelastic mass splitting into a correlated future-collider target.

papers.title: LZ Nuclear-Recoil Excess from Boosted Light Magnetic Dipole-dipole Dark Matter
papers.summary: The authors argue that boosted light dark-sector particles with magnetic dipole-dipole scattering can harden the recoil spectrum, reduce the unwanted low-energy rate, and reproduce the LZ candidate with masses extending to the GeV scale.
papers.takeaway: Uses a boosted population to rescue a momentum-dependent elastic spectrum without TeV halo dark matter.

papers.title: Solar Capture Tests of Inelastic Dark Matter after the LZ High-Recoil Event
papers.summary: The authors compare solar-capture limits for three LZ-motivated endothermic models, excluding the canonical thermal Higgsino benchmark while finding that the tested pseudo-Dirac and neutron-philic spin-dependent cases remain below adopted IceCube limits.
papers.takeaway: Narrows the solar-neutrino challenge to fixed-strength Higgsino interpretations rather than all endothermic models.

papers.title: Inelastic Self-interacting Dark Matter and LUX-ZEPLIN 248 keV Event in a Dirac Modular Inverse Seesaw
papers.summary: The authors place an endothermic pseudo-Dirac self-interacting dark-matter fit inside a modular inverse-seesaw model, linking the required splitting to neutrino masses and to a possible gravitational-wave signal from domain-wall annihilation.
papers.takeaway: Connects the recoil mechanism to neutrino structure, self-interactions, and a gravitational-wave signature.

papers.title: High-Energy Nuclear Recoils from Boosted Dark Matter for the LZ 248-keV Event: Beyond the Halo-Dependent High-Velocity Tail
papers.summary: The authors propose light boosted dark matter whose energy is set by dark-sector masses, using either momentum-dependent elastic scattering or near-threshold inelastic scattering to confine recoils away from both LZ sidebands.
papers.takeaway: Replaces the uncertain halo tail with a boosted flux and sharply defined recoil endpoints.

papers.title: Inelastic B-L scalar dark matter and the LUX-ZEPLIN event
papers.summary: The authors show that an inelastic scalar in a gauged B-L model can match the event near a resonant thermal-relic region and predict a gauge-boson resonance that can test the required coupling and mass scale.
papers.takeaway: A resonant scalar-dark-matter explanation with a linked collider target.

papers.title: A Dark-Dimension Origin of Geometric Inelastic Dark Matter: The LUX-ZEPLIN High-Recoil Event and Multi-Target Tests
papers.summary: The authors derive the few-hundred-keV splitting of a pseudo-Dirac electroweak doublet from warped extra-dimensional localization, fit the LZ recoil region, and predict that tungsten remains accessible while lighter targets do not.
papers.takeaway: Gives the inelastic splitting a geometric origin and a heavy-target discriminator.

papers.title: Pseudo-Dirac Inelastic Dark Matter in the Leptophobic U(1)_B Model: Confronting the LUX-ZEPLIN High-Recoil Event with Collider Searches
papers.summary: The authors use gauged baryon number to generate both dark-state stability and an off-diagonal current, identifying LZ-compatible thermal benchmarks whose mediator lies close to current or projected dijet-search reach.
papers.takeaway: An over-constrained leptophobic construction that can be tested with Run-3 and HL-LHC dijet data.

papers.title: LZ nuclear recoil event from inelastic singlet-doublet scalar dark matter
papers.summary: The authors study mixed singlet-doublet scalar dark matter and find regions consistent with the relic abundance and elastic limits that also yield an endothermic recoil rate and energy compatible with the LZ candidate.
papers.takeaway: Broadens electroweak-doublet explanations through scalar singlet mixing.

papers.title: Boosted dark particles and the LZ nuclear recoil event
papers.summary: The authors interpret the event as elastic scattering of a boosted dark-sector particle with momentum-dependent pseudoscalar interactions, predicting little annual modulation, no leading argon signal, and complementary recoils in spinful light nuclei.
papers.takeaway: A boosted elastic alternative with target and modulation signatures distinct from halo inelastic dark matter.

papers.title: Inelastic Singlet-Doublet Fermion Dark Matter in light of the 248 keV LZ event
papers.summary: The authors use a singlet-doublet fermion sector in which Majorana splitting suppresses elastic Z exchange while retaining endothermic scattering, and connect the splitting mechanism to a scalar triplet that also generates neutrino masses.
papers.takeaway: Links an electroweak inelastic fit to a Type-II seesaw origin for neutrino mass.

papers.title: Not so good νs for Higgsino dark matter as LZ excess: stringent limits from Super-Kamiokande and IceCube
papers.summary: The authors use atmospheric-neutrino measurements from Super-Kamiokande and IceCube to constrain Higgsinos captured in the Sun, reporting a lower splitting bound near 557 keV that disfavors standard-halo Higgsino explanations of the LZ event.
papers.takeaway: An independent solar-neutrino challenge to both thermal and nonthermal Higgsino interpretations.

papers.title: Higgsino Dark Matter Interpretation of the LZ High-Recoil Event in the GNMSSM with TeV-Scale Gauginos
papers.summary: The authors show that Higgsino-Singlino mixing in the GNMSSM can produce sub-MeV neutralino splittings with multi-TeV rather than ultraheavy gauginos, and present relic-compatible benchmarks fitting the LZ likelihood.
papers.takeaway: Realizes the Higgsino-like recoil with accessible gaugino scales, pending a dedicated solar-capture test.

papers.title: From LUX-ZEPLIN to Colliders: Probing Higgsino Dark Matter
papers.summary: The authors trace the 1.1 TeV Higgsino interpretation to a nearly degenerate chargino with a sub-centimeter track, finding current LHC searches insensitive but identifying tracklet reach at future hadron and muon colliders.
papers.takeaway: Translates the LZ-motivated Higgsino spectrum into a short-track collider signature.

papers.title: ALP-mediated inelastic dark matter and the LUX-ZEPLIN high-recoil candidate event LZ230616
papers.summary: The authors model two Majorana states coupled through a gluonic axionlike mediator and find a narrow LZ-compatible spectrum near 350 GeV and a 330 keV splitting, while noting the large coupling product and strong halo-cutoff sensitivity.
papers.takeaway: Combines endothermic kinematics with a momentum-dependent axion portal and exposes its main consistency tests.

papers.title: A Vector-Like Lepton Interpretation of the High-Energy Nuclear Recoil Candidate in LUX-ZEPLIN
papers.summary: The authors fit the hard recoil with elastic spin-dependent scattering in singlet-doublet Majorana dark matter, using a Higgs blind spot to suppress low-energy spin-independent recoils while retaining a thermal-relic region.
papers.takeaway: A viable elastic spin-dependent alternative with complementary solar-neutrino tests.

papers.title: Endothermic dark matter with a light dark photon and the LUX--ZEPLIN high-energy nuclear-recoil candidate
papers.summary: The authors jointly scan the LZ energy likelihood and relic density for endothermic dark matter with a light kinetically mixed dark photon, finding TeV masses and few-hundred-keV splittings while highlighting late-time excited-state constraints.
papers.takeaway: A likelihood-based dark-photon fit whose viability depends on depleting the long-lived excited state.

papers.title: Neutron disappearance and the LZ nuclear recoil event
papers.summary: The authors interpret the recoil as disappearance of a bound xenon neutron, either spontaneously or through a dark-matter-induced reaction, and derive quiet-event fractions, oxygen constraints, and line-like behavior near threshold.
papers.takeaway: A nuclear-disappearance alternative that can be tested through target dependence and accompanying activity.

papers.title: For Whom the Xenon Recoils: Magnetic Inelastic Dark Baryons
papers.summary: The authors construct composite dark-baryon dark matter with an inelastic magnetic transition, find that TeV-scale masses and 100–500 keV splittings can fit the LZ event across several halo models, and predict an accompanying photon signal for some recoils.
papers.takeaway: A composite magnetic-inelastic explanation with a coincident-photon discriminator.

papers.title: A Warped Extra Dimensional Candidate for the LZ 248 keV Event
papers.summary: The authors construct a warped-extra-dimensional pseudo-Dirac fermion whose localized masses naturally generate a roughly 300 keV splitting and whose dark gauge mediator can fit the LZ event while evading fixed-coupling Higgsino tensions.
papers.takeaway: Uses geometric suppression to obtain the splitting and decouple the rate from the minimal Higgsino prediction.

papers.title: Mixing-suppressed inelastic dark matter: a minimal model for the LZ 248 keV event
papers.summary: The authors use singlet-doublet mixing to suppress the Z-mediated inelastic rate without pushing the splitting deep into the halo tail, and study relic abundance, solar capture, cooling, and IceCube limits near the thermal endpoint.
papers.takeaway: Trades extreme-threshold suppression for mixing suppression while retaining correlated solar and relic tests.
